scope: Corollary 1.3 (Planar k-sets and straight-line levels) of the manuscript “A power saving for planar halving lines” (preprints/A-power-saving-for-planar-halving-lines-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 183 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 61d7aa1ffad4b796), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants ε0 > 0 and C0 < ∞ such that, for every integer n ≥ 2 and every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2, the number of k-sets of any n-point set Q ⊂ R2 with no three collinear is at most C0n(k + 1)1/3−ε0 . (1.1) The same bound holds for comp(Λk(L)) for any arrangement L of n nonvertical straight lines with no parallel pair and no three concurrent.
